term: commission: reported commission versus Jesus' commissioning
resolution: The five report statements (STMT-REPORTED-MATT-16-CHURCH-ON-ROCK-KEYS-BINDING, STMT-REPORTED-MATT-18-CHURCH-JUDGES-DISCIPLES-BIND, STMT-REPORTED-MATT-COMMISSION-GROUNDED-IN-GIVEN-AUTHORITY, STMT-REPORTED-JOHN-20-SENDING-FORGIVE-RETAIN, STMT-REPORTED-JOHN-21-PETER-SHEPHERD) use the textual sense: what a Gospel says Jesus gave (DEF-COMMISSION-REPORT-POWERS). STMT-COMMISSION-REPORTS-GO-BACK-TO-JESUS uses both senses and is the only bridge between them: it asserts that the event (Commissioning.Gave, DEF-COMMISSION-EVENT-AND-GOVERNING-POWER) happened for the powers the reports name. STMT-CHURCH-FOUNDED-IN-COMMISSIONED-APOSTLES uses only the event sense. No step passes from a report to an event except through that report-to-event premise, and the substance of a commission (its powers) is meant, not its wording. A critical dating of a saying to 'a later period' or 'after Easter' (STMT-MATT-18-17-JUDGING-SAYING-LATER) is read in the event sense: the community, not Jesus, formed the saying, so Jesus did not give (or promise) the power; that inference from the dating to the event is the reading of the claim stating it (HARNACK-HOD-I-II-3-N76-CHURCH-SAYINGS-LATER), not the dating's own content. It is not the report's own post-resurrection setting: a power the risen Jesus gave (John 20.21-23, Matthew 28.18-20) counts as Jesus' giving in Commissioning.Gave.
